title: Jesus and Nicodemus. Part 4
scripture_text: ‘’Now there was a Pharisee, a man named Nicodemus who was a member of the Jewish ruling council. He came to Jesus at night and said, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God. For no one could perform the signs you are doing if God were not with him.” Jesus replied, “Very truly I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again.’’ ‘’How can someone be born when they are old?” Nicodemus asked. “Surely they cannot enter a second time into their mother’s womb to be born!” Jesus answered, “Very truly I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit. Flesh gives birth to flesh, but the Spirit gives birth to spirit. You should not be surprised at my saying, ‘You must be born again.’ The wind blows wherever it pleases. You hear its sound, but you cannot tell where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit. “How can this be?” Nicodemus asked. “You are Israel’s teacher,” said Jesus, “and do you not understand these things? Very truly I tell you, we speak of what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, but still you people do not accept our testimony. I have spoken to you of earthly things and you do not believe; how then will you believe if I speak of heavenly things? No one has ever gone into heaven except the one who came from heaven—the Son of Man. Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes may have eternal life in him. For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through him.’’
devotional:
Verses 5-8 have caused a lot of debate among theologians as to what Jesus meant when he spoke about being ‘born of the water and the Spirit.’. Jesus is dealing with Nicodemus and he is surprised by Nicodemus’ response to what Jesus has said. ‘You should not be surprised at my saying you must be born again.’ The word used for surprised is thaumazo, which means to be astonished, and it is where we get our English word traumatic from. Jesus is conscious that Nicodemus is really struggling. So Jesus presents the same truth but in different language. Knowing that Nicodemus was ‘Israel’s teacher’ and was very well versed in the Old Testament, Jesus uses the symbolism of the Old Testament to try and communicate the truth to Nicodemus. There are several Old Testament texts that use the symbolism of water and wind to refer to the new life the Spirit gives.

Isaiah 44:3-5

‘’For I will pour water on the thirsty land,

and streams on the dry ground;

I will pour out my Spirit on your offspring,

and my blessing on your descendants.

They will spring up like grass in a meadow,

like poplar trees by flowing streams.

Some will say, ‘I belong to the Lord’ others will call themselves by the name of Jacob;

still others will write on their hand, ‘The Lord’s,’and will take the name Israel.

Ezekiel 36:24-27

“For I will take you out of the nations; I will gather you from all the countries and bring you back into your own land. I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean; I will cleanse you from all your impurities and from all your idols. I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit in you; I will remove from you your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh. And I will put my Spirit in you and move you to follow my decrees and be careful to keep my law.’’

To be ‘Born again’ is to experience the work of the Holy Spirit producing new life. To be born of water and the Spirit is talking about one thing and it may well be referring to the cleansing and empowerment that comes through the new birth.

To help us understand the new birth, let us consider some of its consequences.

The new birth rescues our humanity. Before we become Christians, our sin has robbed us of the glory of our humanity. The new birth makes us more human, it increases our ability to fulfil our creator’s intention.

Being born again is to have a new identity, it is to have a new source of life, it is an understanding that nothing on earth can give you value or significance. It is so radical that you no longer depend on success, reputation or accomplishment to give you value. We will never become the people God wants us to be until we experience the new birth.

Being born again is to recognise that we are primarily spiritual creatures not physical. We have very real physical needs, we need food, clothes, shelter, heat, water, etc. However, while our physical needs may sustain life, they can never give live. We only come fully alive when we experience the regeneration of the Spirit of God.

Being born again means we can experience the Kingdom of God. Often when we read the phrase Kingdom of God we assume it is referring to heaven. But it’s not. Heaven may be a part of the Kingdom of God, but it is not the whole Kingdom of God. The kingdom of God is where God rules, where God is King. Being born again is having a character that longs to completely submit to God. It is finding great joy in absolute surrender, which is something that someone who is not a new creation would ever want to do.

Being born again will help us understand and accept ourselves. Often the problem with self-acceptance is that we don’t know who we are or who we should be. The new birth is where the journey of authenticity begins, for through it, we begin to become the person God has designed us to be, and the person we have always wanted to be; someone who knows they are accepted and loved.

Being born again will change how you view the world. We live in a world where power, position, prestige and possessions are important, they become symbols of our significance and value. This was like the world Nicodemus lived in.

Power, position, prestige and possessions feel important when we are feeling insecure or unloved. However, being born again into the family of God, should cause us to feel loved and secure because we have been born into a loving family with a loving father.

Being born again is the goal of the love of God. God gave his Son to die a cruel death on the cross so we could become new people. It is as if God’s pursuing love finds it’s intimate satisfaction in the new birth of those he has created. I don’t know if you have ever been at a birth, for most it is a wonderful, joyful experience, although it is not easy for the mother. The joy of such an experience is a pale shadow of how God feels about a person being born again.

Being born again means that we don’t ever need to live under condemnation. The new people we become through being born from above/again is designed to live completely free from condemnation. ‘God did not send his Son into the world to condemn it,’ condemnation is the antithesis to the new birth, and will stop growth and maturity.

This meeting Nicodemus had with Jesus was very disturbing for him. Nicodemus had a set of fixed ideas of what a Messiah should be like. Jesus says something that totally destroys Nicodemus’ understanding and theology. Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up that everyone who believes may have eternal life in him.”For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.’ When we read the words ‘For God so loved the world,’ we often mistakenly think that this verse is talking about the extent of God’s love, how much he loves the world. But that is not the writer’s intention. When we read ‘God so loved the world, the writer is referring back to verse 14. Jesus uses the story of Moses lifting up the snake in the wilderness from Numbers 21:4-9 to illustrate his death. This is a strange story and disturbing story, where Jesus compares his death on the cross with a bronze snake, I find this a bit uncomfortable. In this story snakes were used as a curse sent by God on his people for their ingratitude and rebellion. The snake equalled a curse, and on the cross Jesus became cursed for us. God loved the world so much that he gave His Son to bear the curse for us.

Here is the point, Nicodemus would have never conceived of a suffering Messiah, or a saviour who would die for others. Nicodemus wanted a Jesus who fitted neatly into his categories, his understanding, The Jesus he wanted, and the Jesus who is, were very different, it is only through the new birth are we able to accept Jesus for who he is, and not try and make him something we think he should be.
prayer: Father thank you for the glories of the new birth.
